description: Faithful capture of the live FamilySearch Wiki United_States_Census_1900 page (built from the wiki-query-api's own returned text, not hand-written), 7088 chars probed 2026-10-02. Serves the per-year follow-up the search-records Step 2 pre-work block names when the country page does not settle which fields that year's schedule collected. LIST THIS BEFORE wiki-read-united-states-census in a test's mcp_fixtures: dispatch takes the first matching predicate, and the generic `~United_States_Census` also matches this URL, so a generic-first order silently serves the country page for a per-year request and the agent cannot tell.

# United States Census 1900



[United States](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Genealogy "United States Genealogy")

[U.S. Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Census "United States Census")

*1900 Census*

[![NARA logo circular black on white](/en/wiki/img_auth.php/thumb/e/ed/NARA_logo_circular_black_on_white.jpg/200px-NARA_logo_circular_black_on_white.jpg)](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/index.php?title=File:NARA_logo_circular_black_on_white.jpg&filetimestamp=20190221173131&)

## Online Resources

* **1900** [United States Census, 1900](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1325221) at FamilySearch
* **1900** [1900 United States Federal Census](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7602) at Ancestry ($)
* **1900** [U.S. Census 1900](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/us-census-1900) at Findmypast ($)
* **1900** [1900 United States Federal Census](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-10131/1900-united-states-federal-census) at MyHeritage ($)

### Maps

* **1900** [FS Catalog Collection](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/4092225)(*) at FamilySearch Catalog
* **Pre-1900** [Ward Maps of United States Cities: Microfilm Reproduction of 232 Maps Described in Ward Maps of United States Cities](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/373717)(*) at FamilySearch Catalog

## Indexes and Images

For an article about 1900 census population schedules available for free online at [FamilySearch Historical Record Collections](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/FamilySearch_Historical_Record_Collections "FamilySearch Historical Record Collections") see the [U.S. Census Population Schedules, 1900](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Census_Population_Schedules,_1900_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records "United States Census Population Schedules, 1900 - FamilySearch Historical Records") Wiki page. Ancestry.com (subscription site) has indexes and images of all 1900 federal censuses. HeritageQuestOnline.com (subscription site) has indexes and images of all 1900 federal censuses. A [Soundex](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Soundex "Soundex") index for each state and for institutions is also available on microfilm.

## Content

The 1900 Census was taken beginning 1 June 1900, for thirty days or two weeks for populations of 10,000+. The following information was recorded by the census taker:

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| * Name * Address * Relationship to head of household * Color/race * Sex | * Month and year of birth * Age at last birthday * Marital status * Number of years married * Total children born to mother | * Number of children living * Birthplace * Birthplace of parents * Foreign born * Year of Immigration * Number of years in U.S. | * Citizenship status of over 21 * Occupation * Read, write & speak English * Home owned or rented * Home was a farm * Home was mortgaged |

## Value

The 1900 census can be used to:[[1]](#cite_note-1)

1. identify month of birth
2. identify year of marriage
3. determine year of immigration

* [Clues in Census Records, 1850-1940](https://www.archives.gov/research/census/1850-1940)

## Unique Features and Problems

1. Month and year of birth
2. Number of years married
3. Number of children born and living
4. How long immigrant been in country and if naturalized
5. Home/farm was owned/rented
6. Property free or mortgaged
7. Person Civil War Vet or widow of one
8. A [Soundex](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Soundex "Soundex") index is available for each state.
9. Oklahoma census schedules and [Soundex](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Soundex "Soundex") indexes are split between Oklahoma Territory to the northwest, and Indian Territory to the southeast.

[![Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory on 1900 census](/en/wiki/img_auth.php/0/0a/Oklahoma1900.png)](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/index.php?title=File:Oklahoma1900.png&filetimestamp=20080722142946& "Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory on 1900 census")

## States and Territories Covered

All states, District of Columbia, and the Territories listed below:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| * [Arizona](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Arizona_Census "Arizona Census") * [Alaska](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alaska_Census "Alaska Census") (unorganized) * [American Samoa](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/American_Samoa_Census "American Samoa Census") (U.S. armed forces) * [Cuba](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Cuba_Census "Cuba Census") (U.S. armed forces) * [Guam](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Guam_Census "Guam Census") (U.S. armed forces) * [Hawaii](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Hawaii_Census "Hawaii Census") | * [New Mexico](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_Mexico_Census "New Mexico Census") * Oklahoma — split between   * [Oklahoma Territory](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Oklahoma_Census "Oklahoma Census")   * [Indian Territory](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Oklahoma_Census "Oklahoma Census") * [Philippines](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Philippines_Census "Philippines Census") (U.S. armed forces) * [Puerto Rico](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Puerto_Rico_Census "Puerto Rico Census") (U.S. armed forces) |

## Missing Records

* **No States Missing**
* **Six million Agriculture Schedules from the 1900 Census were destroyed by order of the 66th United States Congress**[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## References

1. [↑](#cite_ref-1) Szucs, Loretto Dennis and Sandra Hargreaves Luebking. *The Source: A Guide book to American Genealogy*. 3rd ed. (Provo, UT: Ancestry, 2006.)
2. [↑](#cite_ref-2) House of Representatives, 66th Congress, 2nd Session, "List of Useless Papers in the Bureau of the Census" in "Document No. 460," p. 1.
